title: The Lee-Yang property of the Blume-Capel model
abstract: The Lee-Yang theory is based on the theorem concerning a property of the ferromagnetic Ising model partition function proved by T. D. Lee and C. N. Yang in 1952. It provides powerful tools for understanding the very nature of phase transitions and critical phenomena in various spin and similar models. Sometimes, this theory is applied to models for which the theorem's validity has not been proved. By the main result of E. H. Lieb and A. D. Sokal, Commun. Math. Phys. 80, 153 (1981), for a given ferromagnetic model, this validity is guaranteed by the same property of the single-spin partition function. Due to the anisotropy term $\sum_i ΔS_i^2$, the single-spin partition function of the Blume-Capel model fails to have the Lee-Yang property for $βΔ> \ln 2$. In this article, we show that the ferromagnetic interaction in such a model can induce the Lee-Yang property, even for these values of $βΔ$. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first result of this kind.
summary: This paper tackles the Lee-Yang property for the Blume-Capel model, a system whose behavior is theoretically challenging due to its anisotropy term. The authors prove that strong ferromagnetic interactions can mathematically restore this crucial property—which governs phase transition analysis—even in parameter regimes where standard theorems predict failure. This provides significant theoretical insight into the critical nature of complex spin systems.
main_problem: The central problem is extending the Lee-Yang property—a condition on the zeros of the partition function related to phase transitions—to the Blume-Capel model in regimes where standard theorems fail.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that the ferromagnetic interaction can induce the Lee-Yang property for the Blume-Capel model even when the single-spin anisotropy term ($ eta\Delta$) exceeds the threshold guaranteed by existing theorems.
method: The analysis employs advanced mathematical techniques involving differential operators, stability conditions on derived functions (like $\Psi$), and relating these to the partition function zeros in the thermodynamic limit.
model_or_system: The system is the Blume-Capel model, an extension of the Ising spin model with spins $S_i \in \{-1, 0, +1\}$, governed by a Hamiltonian including nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic interactions ($J_{ij}$) and a single-ion anisotropy term ($\Delta S_i^2$).
key_observables: The Lee-Yang property itself (zeros of the partition function lying on the unit circle) is the key diagnostic, alongside the stability of derived functions $G$ and $\Psi$.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the coupling constants ($J_{ij}$), the anisotropy field ($\Delta$), and the inverse temperature ($ eta$). The critical regime involves comparing $ eta\Delta$ to $\ln 2$.
main_assumptions: The results are presented as sufficient conditions; the proof relies on establishing the stability of certain mathematical constructs derived from the partition function, which is an extension beyond the strict bounds of existing theorems.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the phase diagram of the BC model and compares simulation/theoretical predictions for transition lines. Other figures compare different functions related to the Lee-Yang property across varying parameters.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon the established Lee-Yang theory, first identifying the failure point in the BC model ($ eta\Delta > \ln 2$). It then develops a mathematical framework using differential operators and stability analysis (Chunks 1 & 2) to prove that ferromagnetic interactions can restore the property. Finally, it discusses specific lattice cases and limitations (Chunk 3).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant for theoretical physicists studying phase transitions in complex quantum or classical spin systems, as understanding when such mathematical properties hold dictates the reliability of mean-field approximations and critical exponents.
